acceptance.given: Subjects, Probes, Matrix Cases, Consumers, and rollback stages participate in one Toolchain evaluation or rollback workflow.

oracle.expected: The isolation boundary check shows independently controlled mutable state and evidence for every listed component, with no cross-component contamination path.
forbidden: Any listed component shares mutable state with another listed component.
Cross-component mutable-state sharing permits one component to alter another component's execution or result.
oracle.observable: The isolation-boundary inspection and the cross-component substitution witness evaluated during matrix execution.

acceptance.then: Each component operates only on independently controlled mutable state and evidence.
acceptance.when: The Toolchain runs or rolls back the participating components and evaluates the isolation boundary.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Inject a cross-component mutable evidence substitution and require the isolation check to reject it.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Partition mutable state and evidence for Subjects, Probes, Matrix Cases, Consumers, and rollback stages, rejecting cross-component evidence substitution.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Existing replay results remain compatible; contamination is rejected rather than represented as success.

slice_hint.state_transition: Shared evaluation workflow with isolation required -> independently owned mutable state and evidence for all participating components.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The boundary check rejects a cross-component state or evidence substitution and finds no mutable-state sharing among the listed components.

acceptance.given: A TC-D1 scope proposal identifies an evaluation-set member for admission while all other scope inputs remain unchanged.

oracle.expected: The scope evaluator rejects the proposal, emits a non-authorizing scope-boundary result, and does not admit the member.
forbidden: An evaluation-set member is admitted, accepted, promoted, or recorded as part of TC-D1 evaluation scope.
A passing replay, seed, matrix, or historical artifact is used as proof that admission is allowed.
oracle.observable: The isolated admission fixture produces a deterministic rejection from the Toolchain scope evaluator.

acceptance.then: TC-D1 proceeds only with non-admitted evaluation candidates.
acceptance.when: TC-D1 scope or implementation work is evaluated.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the isolated TC-D1 evaluation-set-admission proposal through the Toolchain scope evaluator; fail the selector if admission is accepted, promoted, or omitted from the rejection result.

slice_hint.behavior_change: The Toolchain semantic scope gate rejects any TC-D1 proposal that admits an evaluation-set member and emits a non-authorizing rejection without changing evaluation membership.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted evaluation membership, schema, historical record, or lifecycle authority is changed; rollback removes only the current Toolchain admission-rejection guard.

slice_hint.state_transition: A proposed TC-D1 scope change that names an evaluation-set member transitions to a rejected, non-authorizing scope result; TC-D1 evaluation membership remains unchanged.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The isolated evaluation-set-admission fixture is rejected by the Toolchain semantic scope gate, records no admission or promotion, and leaves the evaluation membership unchanged.

acceptance.given: A frozen non-empty Consumer Manifest and the reconciled repository real-call surface, including VDD, Acceptance, and workflow-model-routing consumers, are available.

oracle.expected: Every applicable Consumer completes enable, disable, rollback, and re-enable through its real call surface; rollback observes the Prior Route identity and Prior Behavior Baseline verdict and diagnostic category.
forbidden: A manifest entry lacks a reconciled real caller.
Configuration-only switching is accepted as rollback.
oracle.observable: Per-Consumer transition call receipts and the bidirectional Consumer Manifest/call-surface reconciliation.

acceptance.then: All applicable transitions for every non-empty Consumer Manifest entry are complete.
acceptance.when: The Consumer transition selector executes against the frozen manifest.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute the Consumer transition selector with one applicable real-call-surface transition omitted or unreachable.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Reconcile the complete non-empty Consumer Manifest bidirectionally with the repository real-call surface, then require each applicable Consumer to execute enable, disable, rollback, and re-enable through its real interface.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing Consumer routes and require rollback to reproduce the bound Prior Route identity, verdict, and diagnostic category.

slice_hint.state_transition: Frozen manifest with applicable transitions pending -> every applicable Consumer has real-call receipts for enable, disable, rollback, and re-enable.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The selector proves 100% transition completion for the reconciled non-empty manifest and rejects omissions, unreachable consumers, and configuration-only rollback.

acceptance.given: A frozen RED descriptor, its bound assertion and failure identity, and a pytest case report produced for that descriptor are supplied to the Toolchain evidence validator.

oracle.expected: The validator accepts failure evidence only when the report is complete, belongs to the same run and RED descriptor, binds the declared assertion and failure identity to an executed call-phase failure, and is reread before a successor stage uses it.
forbidden: A fabricated RED report is accepted.
A post-hoc or replayed failure report is accepted.
A setup, teardown, harness, skipped, xfail, or unbound failure establishes defect-revealing RED discipline.
oracle.observable: The selected Toolchain test observes deterministic rejection for independently mutated report lineage and for a failure marker that is not an executed behavioral assertion failure.

acceptance.then: Fabricated and post-hoc failure evidence cannot establish required defect-revealing test discipline.
acceptance.when: RED or failure evidence is evaluated.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Mutate the RED case report's run or descriptor binding, completion state, call event, or report hash and require evidence admission to reject it.
Supply a failure marker from setup or a non-behavioral failure after the RED descriptor is frozen and require the RED evidence check to reject it as not proving the declared behavioral assertion.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Require Toolchain RED evidence admission to bind a completed case report to its frozen descriptor, run, declared assertion, failure identity, and executed call-phase behavioral failure; require successor-stage rereading of that binding so fabricated, replayed, or post-hoc failure material cannot establish defect-revealing discipline.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve the existing Quick Dev descriptor, process-receipt, case-report, and stage-result schemas; invalid or stale RED evidence remains non-authorizing and cannot become successor proof.

slice_hint.state_transition: A claimed RED failure without a current descriptor/run/report/call-phase binding transitions to evidence rejection instead of admissible defect-revealing evidence.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Both forged-report lineage and post-hoc or non-behavioral failure-marker selectors are rejected, and no successor stage can use either as valid RED evidence.
